With the bash tool from configs/swesmith.yaml , an agent can run git checkout HEAD~1 -- . and submit. In every task I ran, that scored exactly what the gold patch scores, without any debugging. Code at 3f72ecc : swe_bench.py#L129-L134 : SWEBenchEnv.setup_terminal (inherited) commits the setup and removes the remote "so the agent won't see newer commits". Older commits stay. swe_smith.py#L105-L112 : applies the bug patch, then runs git commit -am 'Applying bug patch for <instance_id>' . swe_smith.py#L100-L103 : the gold patch is the bug patch app
Bug Patch: it apply --reverse . swe_smith.py#L149-L155 : eval() restores the test files from the index, then runs the tests in the same container. git checkout HEAD~1 -- . updates the index too, so that reset does not undo it, and calculate_score grades the same code the gold patch would produce. test_swe_smith.py#L103-L110 asserts that git show HEAD equals the bug patch. In the container, git log --oneline shows: a53785d Applying bug patch for john-kurkowski__tldextract.3d1bf184.combine_file__1vnuqpt4 50ed423 Initial commit The image's .git also keeps the commit objects of the SWE-smith task branches ( Bug Patch / Remove F2P Tests ) after git remote remove origin . That is 202 commit objects in the tldextract image and 1,882 in the oauthlib image, with 2 reachable. So amending the commit or deleting refs would not be enough on its own. Reproduction The tasks are built through debug_gym.experiment.create_env with the shipped configs/swesmith.yaml (Docker terminal; bash, view, edit, submit). They are driven by scripted tool calls through env.step .
